text:
Lars Eller scored the winner on a 3% chance. With 2:23 left in the third, his wrist shot from Aaron Ekblad's pass beat Spencer Knight and gave FLA a 3-2 win at the United Center. Eller was drafted 13th overall by the Blues in 2007 out of Frolunda Jr., and a goal that unlikely is the sort of thing a veteran gets by simply being there when the puck comes loose.

Our numbers say the game was closer than the winning goal makes it look. On expected goals (the quality of chances, not just the count), FLA led 3.86 to 3.31, and shot attempts were even at 60 apiece. But CHI's total includes 1.10 from seven power plays that produced nothing, while FLA's 0.52 on four chances yielded Matthew Tkachuk's tip-in. In a simulation of every shot replayed, CHI wins slightly more often, 51% to 49%, so we'd call this a coin flip that went FLA's way. The first period belonged to FLA, who out-chanced CHI 1.70 to 0.97 and led 2-1 after Sandis Vilmanis and Tkachuk answered Ryan Greene's opener. CHI took the second, and Roman Kantserov tied it at 2-2. He scored 36 goals in 63 KHL games for Metallurg Magnitogorsk last season, and this one came on a wrist shot with Patrick Kane and Connor Bedard assisting.

The goaltending tilted it. Akira Schmid made 19 saves on 21 shots and stopped about 1.3 more goals than the chances against him deserved (goals saved above expected), while Knight finished almost exactly on par at 30 saves on 33 shots. Our data doesn't give us streaks or standings for either side, so what we can say is that FLA leave Chicago with the points after a night that was less comfortable than the shot count (33-21) suggests, and CHI have a lopsided power-play count to think about.
